advisories.title: Carried from v1 — no failsIf and no whatThisCloses block
advisories.detail: The artifact still exposes none of its own claims to refutation and carries no closure block, so a reader cannot see in one place that acceptance would close nothing by itself and that OBL-FX-AUTHORING remains. It does name the obligation in purpose and doesNot, and v2 adds a lands declaration naming the finding it folds, which is a partial improvement on the same axis — a reader can now see what this turn claims to have done, just not what remains after it. This is a family-wide convention gap across the doctor-fc and permission-fx catalogs rather than anything specific to this artifact, and it is not a reason to author a v3.

consideredAndDeclined.candidate: The five assert fields on the state use four different value shapes — a token for recoveryRecords, booleans for three, and NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED for the disclosure assert — which could read as though only the fifth is unauthored
consideredAndDeclined.why: Declined, and I pressed it because it is the one seam the fold introduces. Three of the four shapes predate the fold, so this is the file's existing looseness rather than a new defect, and the authoritative statement is uniform: assertsNamedNotAuthored carries all five under a field name that says all five are named and none authored, at file level and again on the state. A reader cannot conclude the other four are authored without contradicting that list. Faulting the value chosen for a field I myself named in the repair, on a fold that took both routes I offered, would also be goalpost-moving.

That is a family-wide convention gap across these catalogs and not a reason to author a v3. This ACCEPT does not close OBL-FX-AUTHORING; that additionally requires your recording.
